title: prefill+decode: chunked speculative prefill, stage-overlap, kernel scheduler & KV-cache alignment
author: Soham Patel
description: Summary: This PR implements a set of coordinated runtime-level optimizations to reduce end-to-end latency and improve GPU utilization for prefill+decode workloads. The changes are focused on: (1) chunked prefill with speculative issuance for long sequences, (2) stage-overlap between prefill and decode to utilize CPU/GPU concurrently, (3) a lightweight kernel scheduler extension that prioritizes prefills with imminent decode overlap, (4) KV-cache alignment and continuous-batching tweaks to reduce memory thrash and improve hit rates. Motivation: Customers observed 15-40% p99 latency regressions for mixed prefill/decode workloads and lower GPU utilization when many short prefill requests arrive alongside long decodes. This is particularly visible in chat-style workloads where back-to-back prefill+decode calls have a lot of shared prefixes. Approach: - Chunked prefill: break long prefill requests into configurable chunks (default 512 tokens) and allow downstream decode stages to begin on earlier chunks. - Speculative prefill: when a prefix is identical across multiple requests (common in system prompts), issue a speculative KV load for the common prefix and attach a light-weight validation step before decode. - Stage overlap: allow the decode scheduler to begin execution on the first ready chunk while the remaining prefill chunks are still being streamed/compiled; requires new synchronization primitives in the pipeline runtime. - Kernel scheduler: lightweight priority hints are passed to the GPU kernel launcher so that small imminent decode kernels can preempt large background prefill kernels without full kernel preemption (rely on fragmentation windows). - KV-cache alignment: ensure KV cache pages are pinned and cached for the speculative prefix path and add a compacted layout for mixed small/large KV entries to reduce memory copying. - Continuous batching: adjust time-windows for batching to bias slightly towards early-decode candidates to reduce tail latency while keeping throughput. Checklist: - [x] Core chunked prefill runtime + API flags - [x] Speculative prefix path + validation - [x] Kernel scheduler priority hints - [x] KV-cache layout changes + pinning - [x] Continuous batching policy + heuristics - [x] Perf benchmarks added - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs: perf/notes and rollout guidance Backwards compatibility: All changes are behind feature flags (runtime config + env var) and default behavior is unchanged. We add a new runtime flag `PREFILL_CHUNK_SIZE` and `SPECULATIVE_PREFILL_ENABLED`. Benchmarks: Microbench (internal perf lab, r6-24g): - Chat mix (50% short prefill 32 tokens, 50% long prefill 2048 tokens): median latency -8%, p95 -12%, p99 -18%, GPU utilization +22% when speculative prefill enabled and chunk_size=512. - Long-prefill-only: throughput +6% due to reduced KV copying and kernel scheduling. End-to-end customer sim (internal): p99 latency improved from 540ms -> 440ms on avg for mixed workloads. Testing & CI: - Added perf harness scripts: tests/perf/prefill_decode_mix.py - Unit tests cover scheduler logic and KV alignment. - CI matrix ran on linux/gpu with CUDA 12 and ROCm. There was one transient flaky test in early run (kv_cache_eviction_test) which I fixed by increasing a wait timeout and adding a deterministic seed. Rollout plan: - Feature-gated rollout via canary: start with dedicated infra pools (internal canary), then enable on hosted for a subset of customers with opt-in. - Observability: added metrics (prefill_chunks_emitted, speculative_prefill_hits, kernel_priority_inversions) and dashboard in Console. Notes: - The kernel scheduler is intentionally conservative: it uses fragmentation windows rather than preemption; we measured lower overhead vs preemption and avoided GPU driver changes. - Future work: combine with model-quantization-aware kernel selection and prefetching KV pages across model variants.
